clue.text: Laid up or down

parts.note: goods are laid up when put aside for later, and wine is laid down in a cellar to keep: either way it is put away

explanation.walkthrough: Both 'laid up' and 'laid down' (as wine in a cellar is laid down) mean put away for future use, so the whole clue defines the one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something laid up or laid down has been kept in reserve, the past tense of keeping in a store.

clue.text: Filth in America is up — it's past the time to be chirpy

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from the bottom, so backwards
the word for filth is placed inside the abbreviation for America

parts.note: US is the United States of America
filth means dirt
something past the time is late

explanation.surface: A grumble that America has gone dirty and it is too late for cheerfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'is up' reads the contained run (UDIRTS) bottom to top, giving STRIDU. The definition is a verb phrase: to stridulate is to make the chirping sound of insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Crickets and grasshoppers stridulate, making their chirping noise by rubbing body parts together.

clue.text: A stir army nearly created in India

definitions.note: a place in India, a phrase standing for the city's name

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: nearly the whole word: army loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Troops caused a commotion somewhere in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' cuts ARMY to ARM; A STIR plus ARM is rearranged, as 'created' signals. The definition is a loose pointer to a place in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Amritsar is a city in the Punjab, home of the Golden Temple, so it is a place located in India.

clue.text: Dined at an appropriate place, which is natural

parts.note: an inn is a fitting place to eat a meal
dined means ate

explanation.surface: Someone ate somewhere suitable, which came naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'ate at an inn': the place comes first in the answer, then the eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Innate qualities are inborn, the ones that come naturally rather than being learned.

clue.text: Lurking, one man rising against the President

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: taken as written
George Bush, US President when the puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: A lone man rises up in opposition to the President, lurking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' suits a down clue, reading the word upwards to give NAM. The President is George W. Bush, in office when the puzzle was published in 2004.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lying in ambush is hiding in wait to attack, which is what lurking means.

clue.text: Brutal men have no right producing a sedative

indicators.note: the remaining letters are worked into a new product, so rearranged
the letter R, short for right, is removed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Violent men without any rights are given a tranquilliser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have no right' drops R from BRUTAL to leave BUTAL; with MEN, 'producing' rearranges the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nembutal is a trade name for pentobarbital, a barbiturate given as a sedative.

clue.text: Turn over to the state something traditionally bad for the system

definitions.text: something traditionally bad for the system

parts.note: PTO stands for 'please turn over', written at the foot of a page
Maine is a US state

explanation.surface: A call to nationalise something long regarded as harmful to the economy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn over to the state' reads like nationalisation, but it is PTO followed by the US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptomaines were long blamed for food poisoning, so the word is traditionally linked to harm in the body.

clue.text: Number of volunteers is very small

definitions.note: an adjective phrase standing for a noun meaning a tiny amount

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a number
o' is a short form of of, as in o'clock
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Only a handful of people have volunteered.
explanation.walkthrough: The TA is the Territorial Army, the British Army's part-time volunteer reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Not an iota means not the smallest amount, so the word names something very small.

clue.text: Flower of the Bronx

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A bloom grown in a New York borough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is crosswordese for a river, something that flows; the Ebro is a river in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a flower in the sense of a thing that flows, and the Ebro is a Spanish river.

clue.text: Esteem one in armed conflict

indicators.note: the letter for one goes inside the jumbled word
letters in conflict are in disorder, so rearranged

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Respecting a soldier fighting in a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conflict' rearranges ARMED into ADMRE, and 'in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem someone is to regard them highly, the same as to think much of them.

clue.text: Left with threatening air

explanation.surface: Someone departed looking menacing.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry the left side of a shield is called sinister, and the everyday sense is menacing or ominous.

clue.text: It's a big mistake to smack and one could be fired

parts.note: a blunder is a serious error
a smack is a loud kiss, and buss is an old word for a kiss

explanation.surface: Hitting someone is a serious error and could get you sacked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smack' looks like a blow, but here it is a smacking kiss, a buss. 'fired' hints at losing a job, but means shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A blunderbuss is an old short gun with a flared muzzle, so it is a weapon that is fired.

clue.text: Spectacles needed for umpire to take correct course

parts.note: ref, short for referee, is an umpire
R stands for right, which means correct
a course of action is simply an action

explanation.surface: An umpire wearing glasses so he can rule correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: An optician's refraction test measures how the eye bends light, to decide what spectacles are needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasses correct faulty refraction, the bending of light by the eye, so that is what spectacles are needed for.

clue.text: One is proper odd

explanation.surface: A remark that someone is truly strange.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the form for one thing is called singular, and singular also means remarkably strange.

clue.text: Sick to a great degree?

indicators.note: something sick is out of order, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone is very ill indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: An aegrotat is a degree awarded to a student too ill to sit the final exams, so 'Sick' also fits the sense of the whole clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An aegrotat is a university pass granted to a student unable to take exams through illness.

clue.text: Food has gone off, but it'll help to make water available

definitions.text: it'll help to make water available

indicators.note: food that has gone off is spoiled, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: The food is rotten, but someone thinks it will make the water drinkable.
explanation.walkthrough: A shadoof is a pole with a bucket and counterweight used in Egypt and elsewhere to lift water for irrigation.
explanation.definitionFit: A shadoof is a counterweighted lever for raising water from a river, so it makes water available.

clue.text: Not up-to-date, but past it

explanation.surface: Old-fashioned, and too old to be useful.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsolete things are out of date, no longer in use and so past their useful life.

clue.text: Transport provider replaces rail in Spain

indicators.note: read as re-places: the letters are placed again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: In Spain, a new operator takes over the railways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaces' is read as re-places, putting the letters in a new order (AIRL). Spain's E comes from its international car registration code.
explanation.definitionFit: An airline is a company running scheduled flights, so it is a provider of transport.

clue.text: "Amazing Grace" — sermon of hellfire preacher?

indicators.note: something amazing has been turned upside down, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sermon on the hymn Amazing Grace given by a fire-and-brimstone preacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amazing Grace' looks like the hymn title, but 'Amazing' rearranges GRACE together with SERMON. The question mark marks the definition as a playful example.
explanation.definitionFit: A hellfire preacher frightens the congregation with threats of damnation, as a scaremonger spreads alarm.

clue.text: Mysterious message makes nothing clear

parts.note: zero, the letter O, means nothing

indicators.note: the word clear is made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cryptic message that turns out to explain nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' signals a rearrangement, giving RACLE. 'Mysterious' looks like an anagram signal too, but it belongs to the definition: oracles spoke in riddles.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle was a prophecy given by a god through a priestess, usually enigmatic and open to interpretation.

clue.text: Early male requires a mother

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse

explanation.surface: A man of old needs his mum.
explanation.walkthrough: A dam is the female parent of a horse or other livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Adam is the first man, the earliest male of all.

clue.text: She points to a post-viral syndrome

parts.note: E and S are two compass points, east and south
ME is myalgic encephalomyelitis, a chronic fatigue condition often following a virus

explanation.surface: A woman identifies an illness that lingers after a virus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' gives two compass points, E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Esme is a girl's name, so it can stand for a woman, referred to as she.

clue.text: It's miserable to lose backing in meeting

indicators.note: the turned word goes inside the word for a meeting

parts.note: a date is an arranged meeting

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word is reversed

explanation.surface: It is wretched to lose support at a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the verb round to ESOL. 'meeting' is a noun here, a date, not the act of meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolate means utterly wretched and forlorn, so it is a strong synonym for miserable.

clue.text: Barrier against alien — there could be money in it

definitions.text: there could be money in it

parts.note: a wall is a barrier
ET is the alien in the film E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial

explanation.surface: A wall built to keep aliens out could prove profitable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'against' means next to, a common way of joining pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallet is a pocket case for banknotes and cards, so money may be found inside it.

clue.text: Some star in performance

indicators.note: the letters are put on stage in a new arrangement, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Certain stars shine when performing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: SOME STAR rearranged, and maestros are stars of a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestros are distinguished conductors or musicians, the stars of a concert performance.

clue.text: Lawrence Harris rejected for a minor bloomer

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so both names are read backwards

parts.note: T E Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia, known by his initials
Rolf Harris, the entertainer

explanation.surface: A person named Lawrence Harris is turned down over a small mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the run TEROLF backwards. 'bloomer' suggests a blunder but means something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A floret is one of the small flowers making up a composite flower head, so a little bloom.
